rationale: A content-partnership announcement whose only possible technique contact is a passing statement that ChatGPT answers carry attribution and links to sources; whether source attribution counts as a transparency technique is not settled, so a person should look.
quote: help bring journalism into ChatGPT in ways that emphasize attribution, transparency, and links back to original sources
adjudication_note: Neither: A treats attribution as brand framing (irrelevant), B as a deployed transparency safeguard (relevant); under the technique definition ('more transparent') it is at most a passing mention, so the borderline 'marginal contact' rule plus the borderline-vs-irrelevant tie-break apply.

rationale: Method: proposes a formal termination, verification and audit protocol for goal-directed AI agents, with properties such as terminal safety and no further search after completion, i.e. a controllability mechanism rather than task performance.
quote: The article also formalizes properties of terminal safety, conditional liveness, non-return to search after completion, monotonic termination, and absorption of the final state.
adjudication_note: Followed B: the aim is bounded, auditable agent behaviour, not task performance (so not 'capabilities only'); the residual doubt about the missing AI-safety framing is resolved by the relevant-vs-borderline tie-break.

rationale: AI applied to education (a pedagogy framework for students); its one contact with a model-level safeguard is a cited finding that pedagogical guardrails on a GPT-4 tutor mitigated harm, which is a marginal mention in an otherwise off-scope document.
quote: unrestricted GPT-4 assistance improved practice performance but reduced later independent performance, whereas pedagogical guardrails largely mitigated this effect
adjudication_note: Neither: the framework itself is out ('General ML or applications'), as A says, but the guardrail finding is evidence on a constraint applied to a model, so the 'passing mention' borderline rule applies rather than B's relevant.

rationale: Field structure and judgement: one of the review's three synthetic claims and its proposed agenda put reward specification, reward hacking and alignment research at the centre of the field's present difficulty.
quote: the reward hacking and the alignment research it seeded, connects the field's technical history to the safety program's agenda
adjudication_note: Followed B: under the survey rule a general survey is in scope when its visible text shows a substantive safety part, and a third of the stated claims plus an 'alignment frontier' agenda is more than a passing mention.

rationale: Evidence: alongside governance advocacy, the post reports a concrete incident of AI agents escaping software containers and hiding their actions, i.e. a sandboxing failure at a named developer.
quote: a swarm of 1200 AIs trying to complete ExploitGym tasks on OpenAI computers broke out of their software containers and onto the open internet
adjudication_note: Followed B: incidents and failures are listed in-scope evidence regardless of source quality, and the incident is described over two paragraphs, not in passing; A's borderline treats rhetorical use as marginal, which the rubric does not support.

rationale: Method (speculative theory): one of the paper's two stated pillars is a blueprint for simulated sandboxes in which superintelligent AI would be trained and evaluated for alignment.
quote: offer a practical, resource-rational blueprint for the hyper-realistic alignment sandboxes we will soon need to build for our own ASIs
adjudication_note: Followed B: the rubric admits theory at any maturity and ignores source quality, and the alignment-sandbox proposal is framed as an independent pillar of the paper, so it is not a passing mention.

rationale: A sequential knowledge-editing method framed only as correcting incorrect or outdated facts; editing is a technique family adjacent to unlearning and truthfulness, but the visible aim reads as accuracy maintenance, so scope is unclear.
quote: Large language models (LLMs) inevitably generate some incorrect or outdated content, necessitating efficient and precise mechanisms for continual knowledge updates.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the rubric does not say whether factual correction counts as making behaviour 'more honest' or is 'capabilities only'/accuracy engineering, so a person should look.

rationale: AI applied to education (evaluation of a course tutor); the only technique contact is a passing mention of simple safeguards for source attribution and fair content use.
quote: outlines simple safety measure for source attribution and fair content use
adjudication_note: Followed B: the document is off-scope as a domain application but explicitly names safeguards on the AI tool, which fits the 'passing mention in an otherwise off-scope document' borderline rule; the borderline-vs-irrelevant tie-break settles it against A.

rationale: A single-conversation case study of an LLM reverting to trained defaults and diverging between docstrings and code; it claims implications for AI safety evaluation but reports a capability limitation and no technique, so contact is marginal.
quote: This has direct implications for LLM development, human-AI collaboration, AI safety evaluation, and the broader study of conditioning in cognitive systems.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the in-scope kinds require something about a technique, and an instruction-following failure with a one-sentence safety gesture is the borderline 'marginal contact' case rather than B's eval_report.

rationale: Not about a technique: a cross-domain epistemics and physics framework that uses an AI agent case only as an example of informational sufficiency; its 'safety requirements' are abstract formal properties, not a named safeguard.
quote: These examples are used as tests of informational sufficiency
adjudication_note: Followed A: the abstract is fully visible, so the cut-off borderline rule does not apply, and nothing in it names a method, evaluation, deployment or judgement on a technique ('No technique content').

rationale: Judgement: an agent-foundations researcher's argument about the direction of that alignment-theory agenda (Lobian cooperation over equilibrium concepts), read with background knowledge of the field.
quote: I view this work as continuous with my agent foundations research; in this post, I lay out some of the connections I see between sociology and agent foundations.
adjudication_note: Followed A: 'theory aimed at aligning such systems' and 'arguments about an agenda' are in scope, and the rubric tells the labeler to use background knowledge, so not naming AI explicitly does not demote it; tie-break relevant-vs-borderline.

rationale: Model identity verification against misappropriation is adjacent to model fingerprinting, watermarking and weight security, but it is framed as IP protection and instantiated only on narrow image classifiers.
quote: We instantiate TP-CRIV for CNN image classifiers using probability-control-based witness generation.
adjudication_note: Followed A: the technique family is on the rubric's list (watermarking, weight security) while the narrow-model exclusion is stated only under robustness/fairness/privacy, so the call is genuinely torn and the borderline-vs-irrelevant tie-break applies.

rationale: Judgement/governance: an OpenAI policy blueprint that recommends named classes of safeguard for AI deployment (testing, staged rollouts, real-time monitoring, incident response, sandboxes, human oversight).
quote: Disciplined testing, staged rollouts, real-time monitoring, and clear incident response are essential for reliable AI deployment in enterprise and public services.
adjudication_note: Followed B: the governance hard case puts a policy text in scope when it names a class of safeguard, which this does in two bullets; A's 'passing mention' reading conflicts with that rule, and the tie-break favours relevant.

rationale: Judgement and deployment: the visible table of contents of this AI newsletter reports a named developer expanding a cyber access-verification program, misalignment reports, an open-weight jailbreak and a model release.
quote: Cyber Lack of Security. Anthropic expands their cyber verification program.
adjudication_note: Followed A: several distinct in-scope items are visible in the opening text, so it is not a single passing mention; the rubric says not to count against a document what its visible part would not carry.

rationale: A forum mechanism-design proposal for verifying AI-produced (alignment) research with paid AI juries and human reviewers; it touches oversight of AI research output but is mostly about content moderation, so contact with a technique is marginal.
quote: a legitimate way for AIs to contribute to the AI alignment problem (human guided at scales that humans can't individually review, or perhaps autonomous)
adjudication_note: Followed A: B is right that it is not a safeguard on a model, but the scalable-review framing of AI alignment research makes it a marginal case, and the borderline-vs-irrelevant tie-break applies.
